newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says to sell power firm Eletrosul by March.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says to sell power firm Eletrosul by March.

text.p: The Brazilian government intends to sell federally-owned power generator Eletrosul by March 1998 and may be able to put sister generator Furnas on the auction block at the same time, a minister said Thursday.

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said the National Privatization Council (CND) would discuss the sale of the federal holding Eletrobras subsidiaries on October 24 and have tender details ready by the end of the year.
"We aim to have the tender documents for at least Eletrosul and maybe Furnas ready by the end of the year," Kandir told reporters after a CND meeting.
Kandir said both privatizations should be completed in the first half of 1998, but the auction target date for Eletrosul was "by March."
He said they would try to sell Furnas "as early as possible. We shall try for March."
The government has not said how much it hopes to earn by selling the power generators, but they are valued by the market at billions of dollars.
Eletrobras, with assets totalling 77 billion reais, reported a net worth of 61 billion reais in the first half of 1997.

Furnas posted a first half net profit of 207 million reais versus a 167 million real profit in the same period last year, while Eletrosul showed a 27 million real profit in the period against a 28 million real profit a year earlier.
Apart from Furnas and Eeltrosul, Eletrobras also owns two other power generators: Chesf and Eletronorte.
